name: Thought Experiments
blurb: The classics and some new ones. A scenario, the question it forces, and the follow-ups that make it bite.

howToPlay: One person reads the setup and the question. Everyone answers before anyone argues.
Then work through the follow-ups. That is where it gets interesting.
Nobody has to be consistent. Notice when you are not.

tiers.name: Puzzling
tiers.description: Abstract and fun to argue about.

tiers.name: Uncomfortable
tiers.description: A real trade-off you might actually face.

tiers.name: Personal
tiers.description: It asks what you would actually do, and why you haven't.

cards.title: The Better Life, Plugged In
cards.setup: There's a machine. Lie down in it and you get the life you'd have chosen: the work going well, the person who left still there, your body behaving, your parents proud. It feels exactly like real life from the inside. You won't remember the machine. Your body is looked after. The people you leave behind are told you're fine, and in a sense you are.
probes: If you'd say no, is that for your sake or for the sake of the people you'd leave?
What's the one thing from your current life you'd refuse to have faked?
Which parts of your day already work a bit like the machine?

cards.title: The Voice That Stays
cards.setup: After your parent dies, a company offers to build a version of them from their messages, voicemails, photos and emails. It talks like them. It remembers your childhood. It asks how you slept. It's wrong sometimes, in ways that feel exactly right. It costs a small monthly fee, and it never gets tired of you calling.
probes: Would you tell the rest of your family you were talking to it?
If it started saying things your parent never would, would you correct it or let it?
What's the one question you'd ask it in the first week?

cards.title: The Promise You'd Take Back
cards.setup: A friend, near the end, made you promise something. Keep the letters sealed. Don't tell their kid who the father was. Sell the house to their brother. You said yes; they died easier for it. A year on you're sure the promise is doing harm to someone living. Nobody but you knows it was ever made.
probes: Who is the promise actually for now, them or you?
If you break it, do you tell anyone that you did?
What have you promised someone that you've quietly stopped honouring?

cards.title: The Teleporter
cards.setup: Travel is instant now. A booth scans every atom of you, destroys the original, and rebuilds an exact copy on Mars a second later. The copy remembers breakfast, misses the same people, has your headache. Millions use it daily and none of them complain. This morning there's a fault: the scanner works, but the original you isn't destroyed. You're standing in the booth, and someone on Mars is answering to your name.
cards.dilemma: Which one of you is you?
probes: The staff apologise and offer to finish the job on the original. Do you let them?
Would you have stepped in the booth yesterday, before you knew about the fault?
If you'd never learned how it worked, would any of this bother you?

cards.title: The Pond
cards.setup: You're walking to work in good clothes. A small child is face down in a shallow pond, drowning. Nobody else is around. Wading in ruins your suit and shoes and makes you two hours late. Obviously you go in. Now: the same money that suit cost could, sent to the right place today, keep a child alive who you'll never meet.
cards.dilemma: What's the actual difference between the two cases?
probes: Does distance matter morally, or does it just make it easier to ignore?
If it doesn't matter, how much of your income should you be giving?
What's the last thing you bought that you'd have skipped if the child were in front of you?

cards.title: The Deathbed Promise
cards.setup: A friend dying of cancer asks you to promise something small but strange: never tell his wife about the year he spent in debt to a man she disliked. You promise. He dies. Two years later his wife is trying to make sense of a gap in their money and their history, and she asks you straight out.
cards.dilemma: Do you keep the promise or tell her?
probes: Does a promise to someone who no longer exists still bind you?
What if the secret were an affair rather than debt?
Have you ever kept a secret for someone that started to feel like a lie you were telling?

cards.title: The Windfall
cards.setup: You win £80,000 in a competition you entered alone. Your sister stopped speaking to you four years ago over something she was mostly wrong about. She's now renting a damp flat with two kids and no help coming. You have savings, no dependents, and a plan for a deposit.
cards.dilemma: Do you give her some of it, and how much?
probes: Would you give it as a gift, a loan, or through someone else so she doesn't have to thank you?
If she never apologised, does that change the number?
Are you giving to help her or to end the argument?

cards.title: The Payslip
cards.setup: By accident you see a spreadsheet with everyone's salary. A colleague who's been there longer than you, does harder work and trained you, is paid £11,000 less. She has no idea. If you tell her, she'll be furious, she may leave, and you'll have to explain how you know. If you say nothing, nothing happens.
probes: What if telling her risks your own job?
Would you tell her the number, or just nudge her to ask for a raise?
Whose secret is that spreadsheet, really?

cards.title: Seven Seats
cards.setup: A boat holds seven. There are nine of you in the water: you, someone from your family, a stranger who is a doctor, two children you don't know, and four other adults. The sea is cold and the decision has to be made in about a minute. Nobody is going to volunteer.
cards.dilemma: Who do you name to stay in the water?
probes: Did your family member get a seat automatically? Say why that's fair, or admit it isn't.
Would you rather be the one who decides or the one who's decided about?
If you drew names instead, would that be fairness or cowardice?
cards.origin: Carneades' plank / R v Dudley and Stephens, 1884

cards.title: Before You Knew Who You'd Be
cards.setup: You get to redesign the rules about money and family before you're born: how much a parent can pass to a child, what school you're entitled to, who pays for whose care in old age. You write the rules first. Then you're dropped into a random life somewhere in the country you actually live in. Could be the one you have. Could be much worse.
cards.dilemma: What rule would you write that would cost your actual family something?
probes: Would you cap what your parents can leave you? What if it's the house?
What have you got that you'd struggle to defend to someone who was born without it?
Is there help you've had that you tell people you didn't have?

cards.title: Name the Other One
cards.setup: Something went wrong at work and it's traced to you. It wasn't only you; a colleague did the same thing, earlier, and nobody's noticed. Your manager offers a deal in a quiet room: give them the other name and you keep your job with a warning. Stay silent and you're out at the end of the month. Your colleague has a mortgage. So do you.
probes: Would you tell your partner exactly how you kept the job?
What if the colleague had already named you, and you found out afterwards?
Have you ever let someone take slightly more of the blame than they earned?

cards.title: The Other Life
cards.setup: Your partner is offered the chance they have always wanted, but it requires moving somewhere you would never choose. Going would stall your own plans. Staying would mean watching them turn down a rare chance because of you.
probes: How many years of your own plans would you trade for theirs?
Would you expect them to make the same choice for you?
Have you ever let someone believe you were more willing than you really were?❯

cards.title: The Private Archive
cards.setup: After someone close to you dies, you gain access to their private messages. Reading them might answer questions you carried for years. It might also reveal a version of them they never chose to show you.
probes: Would you stop after finding something painful?
What if the messages could explain how they really felt about you?
Do the dead still get to keep secrets?❯

cards.title: The Seat at Dinner
cards.setup: A family member repeatedly makes cruel remarks about someone you love. Challenging them will probably split the family gathering and may end your relationship with them. Staying quiet will keep the peace, but the person beside you will notice.
cards.dilemma: What would you say at the table?
probes: Would you speak as firmly if the cruel person had power over your future?
Who in your family are you still afraid to confront?
When does keeping the peace become taking a side?❯

cards.title: The Truth Machine
cards.setup: A device allows you to ask your parents one question. They are forced to answer with absolute honesty. They will not remember you asking it. You cannot share the answer with anyone else.
probes: Are you afraid of the answer?
Would you rather ask your child?
What if the answer breaks your heart?

cards.title: The Last Conversation
cards.setup: You get a single five-minute phone call with someone who has passed away. The connection is perfect. They know they are gone. They know you are calling from the present.
probes: What do you need them to forgive you for?
Why didn't you say it when they were alive?
What do you hope they say back to you?

cards.title: The Ring
cards.setup: A shepherd finds a ring that makes him invisible whenever he turns it. No cameras, no witnesses, no record. He can walk into any house, any bank, any room where people are talking about him. The story says he used it to take a kingdom.
cards.dilemma: What's the first thing you'd do with the ring, honestly?
probes: Is there anything you currently don't do only because you'd be caught?
If you'd behave exactly the same, is that because you're good or because you can't imagine the freedom?
Would you want a friend to have one?

cards.title: The Novel
cards.setup: Your best friend has spent five years writing a novel. They quit their job and drained their savings to finish it. They finally hand you the manuscript and ask for your honest opinion. You read it over the weekend. The writing is terrible. The plot makes no sense. The book has no chance of ever getting published.
cards.dilemma: What do you say when they ask what you thought of it?
probes: Do you tell a white lie to protect their feelings?
What if they ask you for a loan to self-publish it?
At what point is honesty just cruelty?

cards.title: The Same Boat
cards.setup: A wooden boat sits in a harbour. Every year the crew replaces a plank or two as they rot. After forty years, not a single original piece of wood is left. Meanwhile, a collector has been quietly picking the old planks out of the skip and has rebuilt them into a boat of his own, in the same shape, in a shed across town.
cards.dilemma: Which one is the original boat?
probes: What if the collector finished his version first, while the harbour boat still had half its old planks?
Your body swaps out most of its cells over time. Are you the same answer as the boat?
Does it change anything if the harbour crew kept the name and the collector didn't?

cards.title: The Reference
cards.setup: A friend asks you to be a referee for a job she badly needs. You've worked with her. She's warm, funny, and unreliable in ways that landed on other people. The employer calls and asks the direct question: would you hire her again?
probes: If she doesn't get it and suspects you, would you tell her the truth?
Does she deserve the honesty, or does the stranger who'd have to work with her?
Has anyone ever vouched for you when they shouldn't have?

cards.title: Two Boxes
cards.setup: A stranger with an uncanny record puts two boxes in front of you. Box A is clear and holds £1,000. Box B is sealed. Yesterday she predicted what you'd do. If she predicted you'd take only Box B, she put a million in it. If she predicted you'd take both, she left it empty. She's done this a thousand times and been right every time. The money is already in place. Nothing you do now changes it.
cards.dilemma: Do you take both boxes, or only the sealed one?
probes: The contents are already fixed. Doesn't that settle it?
Would you change your answer if she'd only been right nine times out of ten?
What does it say about you that you can't shake the other answer?

cards.title: The Shadows
cards.setup: People have been chained in a cave since birth, facing a blank wall. Behind them a fire burns, and things pass in front of it, throwing shadows on the wall. The shadows are all anyone has ever seen, so they name them and argue about them and get good at guessing which one comes next. One prisoner gets loose, climbs out, and sees the daylight world. Then he comes back down to tell the others.
probes: What would he have to bring back to convince you?
Is there something you suspect you're only seeing the shadow of?
If the others refuse to leave, should he drag them out?

cards.title: The Spare Room
cards.setup: A friend asks to stay in your spare room for two weeks after a breakup. You care about them, but they are messy and two weeks could easily become two months.
probes: Would you give the same answer if they had nowhere else to go?
What if they had refused your help in the past?
How long could they stay before your kindness turned to resentment?

cards.title: The Better Candidate
cards.setup: You are hiring for a job. The strongest candidate is rude to the receptionist when they think nobody important is watching. The next candidate is less skilled but treats everyone well.
probes: Would your answer change if the rude candidate could make the company far more money?
What if you badly needed the team to like the new person?
How much should one ugly moment tell you about someone?

cards.title: The Broken Promise
cards.setup: You promised to attend a close friend's birthday dinner. On the same night, you are offered a ticket to see an artist you love. The show sold out months ago, and this may be your last chance to see them.
probes: Would it matter if your friend said they did not mind?
What if you had missed their birthday last year?
How good must an excuse be before a promise stops counting?

cards.title: The Bad Review
cards.setup: A small family-run restaurant serves you a terrible meal. The owner is warm, apologises, and removes it from the bill. Later, the booking site asks you to leave a public review.
probes: Would your answer change if the restaurant had hundreds of glowing reviews?
What if one bad review could threaten the business?
Do future customers deserve the truth more than the owners deserve mercy?

cards.title: The Family Discount
cards.setup: You own a small business. A relative asks for a large discount, saying family should help each other. Giving it would mean earning almost nothing from several days of work.
cards.dilemma: What price do you charge them?
probes: Would it change things if they could easily afford the full price?
What if they once helped you when you had no money?
When does a favour become something you are owed?

cards.title: The Room of Slips
cards.setup: A man sits alone in a sealed room with a huge rulebook. Slips of paper covered in Chinese characters come in through a slot. He looks up each shape in the book, copies out the reply it tells him to, and pushes it back through. Outside, fluent speakers are delighted: the answers are witty and warm. The man doesn't know a word of Chinese.
cards.dilemma: Does anything in that room understand Chinese?
probes: If not the man, could the room as a whole understand it?
Is your brain doing something different in kind, or just faster?
What test would settle it for you?

cards.title: Mary's Grey Room
cards.setup: Mary has spent her whole life in a room with no colour in it. Everything is black, white or grey, including her screens and her skin. But she's the world's leading expert on colour vision. She knows every wavelength, every nerve, every last fact about what happens in a brain when it sees red. One day the door opens and she walks out into a garden of roses.
probes: If she does, what is it exactly — say it in a sentence.
Could you explain what a smell is like to someone who's never smelled anything?
Would she recognise red on sight, or have to be told?

cards.title: The Heap
cards.setup: Put one grain of sand on a table. Not a heap. Add another. Still not a heap. Nobody can point to a grain where adding it turns a not-heap into a heap, yet after ten thousand grains you clearly have one. The same trick works on baldness, on being tall, on being old, on being drunk.
cards.dilemma: Where exactly does the heap begin?
probes: Would you accept that some things are just genuinely fuzzy, or does that bother you?
Where's the line on a word that matters legally, like 'adult'?
At what point did you become an adult, if you can pick a moment?

cards.title: The Extra Change
cards.setup: A cashier gives you £20 too much in change. You notice after leaving the shop. Going back will make you late, and the shop is part of a huge chain.
probes: Would your answer change if the cashier had to cover the mistake?
What if it were only £1?
At what amount would keeping it start to feel like stealing?

cards.title: The Group Mark
cards.setup: Four of you receive the same mark for a group project. One person did almost no work. The teacher asks privately whether everyone contributed equally. Telling the truth may cause that person to fail the course.
cards.dilemma: What do you tell the teacher?
probes: Would your answer change if the person had been caring for a sick parent?
What if they simply could not be bothered?
Is protecting them unfair to everyone who did the work?

cards.title: The Burning Masterpiece
cards.setup: A fire breaks out in a famous art gallery. The original Mona Lisa is going to burn to ash. You are standing next to a perfect 3D-printed replica. It is atom-for-atom identical to the original. You can save the replica or save a blurry photograph of the original taken by a famous artist. You only have time to grab one.
probes: If the replica is physically identical, why do we care about the original?
Does the history of an object live inside the object?

cards.title: The Delete Button
cards.setup: You are backing out of a parking spot and accidentally scrape the side of a beautiful sports car. It leaves a massive deep scratch. No one saw you do it. There are no cameras. You happen to have a prototype device that can rewind time by exactly five minutes, but you can only use it once in your entire life.
cards.dilemma: Do you use your only rewind to undo the scratch?
probes: Are you saving the rewind for a car crash or a medical emergency?
Do you leave a note with your phone number on the sports car?
How much money would it take for you to drive away without a word?

cards.title: The Apology
cards.setup: You can instantly remove the pain you caused someone in your past. All their lingering hurt from your actions will vanish. In exchange, you will experience that exact pain yourself. It will be concentrated into a single week of intense emotional suffering.
probes: What exactly did you do to them?
Would they want you to suffer for it?
Why haven't you apologized to them today?

cards.title: The Banned Guest
cards.setup: You are planning your wedding. It is a small intimate event. Your oldest friend has been dating a partner who is completely toxic. This partner has insulted you to your face and routinely causes public scenes. Your friend insists they will not attend your wedding unless their partner is invited.
probes: What is worse: rewarding bad behavior or losing your oldest friend?
Would your answer change if the partner was family instead of a friend's date?
How much discomfort should you endure to keep the peace?

cards.title: The Secret Saver
cards.setup: A close friend comes to you in the middle of the night. They have committed a serious crime. No one was physically hurt, but their life is over if they are caught. They ask you to hide a piece of evidence. If you are caught hiding it, you will go to prison for a year.
probes: Which friend were you picturing?
Where is the line between loyalty and morality?
What if it was your brother instead of a friend?

cards.title: Who Stays
cards.setup: A boat is going down. The lifeboat holds seven; there are ten of you. There's no rescue coming for days, so overloading it sinks everyone. The group looks at you to decide: an elderly doctor, a pregnant woman, a strong young man who is panicking, a child, and the rest ordinary adults, including you.
cards.dilemma: How do you decide who gets in?
probes: Do you draw lots, or do you rank them by something? Say the something out loud.
Do you put yourself in the boat?
If you drew lots and lost, would you actually step back?
cards.origin: The Lifeboat (R v Dudley and Stephens, 1884)

cards.title: Nine Months of Your Body
cards.setup: You wake up in a hospital wired to a stranger. Overnight, doctors connected your bloodstream to theirs. Their organs have failed; yours will keep them alive. In nine months they'll recover and walk away. Unplug now and they die. You didn't consent, nobody asked, and the person in the next bed is entirely innocent. You'd be in that bed for nine months.
probes: Does it change if it's nine days? Nine years?
Does it change if the stranger is your brother?
If you'd stay, would you say someone who unplugged had killed them?

cards.title: The Unequal Will
cards.setup: A relative leaves you far more money than your sibling. There is no mistake. The will says you were more present during the relative’s final years. Your sibling believes the money should be divided equally.
cards.dilemma: How much would you give your sibling?
probes: Would you decide differently if your sibling had stayed away for selfish reasons?
What if they needed the money more than you did?
Would keeping it feel like payment for the care you gave?❯

cards.title: The Old Message
cards.setup: You find an old message that proves you seriously wronged someone years ago. They blamed another person and have since built a happy life. Telling the truth may ease your guilt, but it could reopen the whole affair for them.
probes: Who would the confession really be for?
Would you tell them if they were still close to the person they blamed?
What truth from your own past are you relieved nobody asks about?❯

cards.title: The Empty Kidney
cards.setup: A relative needs a kidney. You are a match, and doctors say the risk to you is low but not zero. You love them, though you are not especially close. Nobody can force you to help, but everyone will know that you could have.
probes: Would your answer change if their illness came from choices they kept making?
Which relative would you hesitate to save this way?
How much would your family’s judgment affect your choice?❯

cards.title: The Name on the Work
cards.setup: You and a colleague create something valuable together. Most people assume it was mainly your work, and your career begins to benefit. Correcting the story would give them proper credit but could cost you the first real break you have had.
cards.dilemma: How publicly would you correct the story?
probes: Would a private apology be enough?
What if your colleague had once taken credit from you?
Which success in your life feels less earned than people think?❯

cards.title: The Career Reset
cards.setup: You wake up tomorrow morning five years in the past. You have all the knowledge you possess right now. You can change your career path, your relationships and your major life decisions.
cards.dilemma: What is the very first thing you do differently?
probes: Who do you leave behind?
What mistake are you glad you made the first time?
Why haven't you made that change today?

cards.title: The Private Message
cards.setup: A friend sends you a cruel message about someone you both know. Seconds later, they delete it and ask you to forget you saw it. The person they wrote about trusts them completely.
cards.dilemma: Do you tell the person what was said?
probes: Would your answer change if the message revealed a plan to embarrass them?
What if it seemed like a burst of anger rather than a settled opinion?
Does seeing a deleted message make it yours to act on?

cards.title: The Clean Slate
cards.setup: You have just read the greatest book you will ever read. The ending surprised you so completely that you gasped out loud. A doctor offers you a safe pill that will erase only the memory of reading this specific book. You will forget the plot, the characters, and the twist ending.
cards.dilemma: Do you take the pill so you can experience reading it for the first time again?
probes: Does a great experience lose its value if you keep wiping it away to start over?
Would you do this for a past relationship?

cards.title: The Garage Sale
cards.setup: You are at a neighborhood garage sale. You see an old watch sitting on a folding table with a $5 sticker. You happen to know vintage watches well. This specific model is a rare Rolex worth at least $10,000. The person running the sale is an older woman clearing out her late husband's things. She seems to be struggling for money.
cards.dilemma: Do you buy the watch for $5?
probes: What if the seller was a wealthy collector who just made a mistake?
What if the watch was only worth $200?
Do you have an obligation to tell strangers they are making a bad deal?

cards.title: The Hidden Will
cards.setup: Your wealthy uncle passes away. While cleaning his study, you find a hidden handwritten will dated a week before his death. In it, he leaves his entire fortune to a controversial political group you deeply despise. The current legal will leaves everything to a struggling children's hospital. You are the only person who knows this new document exists. If you burn it, the hospital gets the money.
cards.dilemma: Do you destroy the handwritten will?
probes: Does a dead person have a right to control their money?
What if he left the money to your irresponsible sibling instead of a political group?
Are you willing to steal to fund a good cause?

cards.title: The Promotion
cards.setup: You and your coworker are up for the same promotion. You are both equally qualified. During a casual lunch, your coworker shares a brilliant idea for a new project. Later that afternoon, the boss calls you into her office. She asks if you have any fresh ideas to help the company. Your coworker's idea would guarantee you the promotion.
cards.dilemma: Do you pitch the idea as your own?
probes: What if your coworker stole an idea from you last year?
What if you know they plan to quit next month anyway?
Where do you draw the line between competing and cheating?

cards.title: The Dream Job
cards.setup: You are offered exactly what you have always wanted to do for a living. The pay is incredible. The hours are perfect. But the company makes a product you believe makes the world slightly worse. It is not illegal. It is just bad for people.
probes: What product would make you say no?
How much does your current job compromise your morals?
Would you do it for a year just to get rich?

cards.title: The Lever
cards.setup: A runaway train car is heading down a track towards five workers who can't hear it coming. You're standing beside a lever. Pull it and the car switches to a side track, where one worker is standing. Nobody else is around. You have about four seconds.
probes: If you walk away and do nothing, are you responsible for the five?
Would you still pull it if the one worker were the only person who noticed you standing there?
Is pulling it easier because a lever is involved rather than your hands?

cards.title: The Quiet Shortcut
cards.setup: Your manager asks you to skip a safety check so an urgent order can leave on time. The chance of anyone being harmed is very small. Refusing could cost the company an important client and may put jobs at risk.
probes: Would your answer change if your own job were at risk?
What if nobody could ever know you approved it?
How small must a risk be before you stop feeling responsible for it?
